script: Entitled neighbor tries storming over demanding access to my Disney+ login information so she can watch a show she wants to watch. This morning my daughter took the dogs outside to let them do their business. They came back before she could scoop the poop, and that's when the neighbor pops up. She's standing like she owns the block and asks, "Does your family have Disney+? I missed a show last night and heard it's on Disney+. Can you give me your login info?" My daughter's like, "No, I can't share that." The neighbor goes, "It's not like your mom would notice." The daughter stays firm. The neighbor gets mad, storms over, and says she's only asking one more time. The daughter says no again. The neighbor leaves, steps right into the poop the daughter was about to pick up, and then screams the loudest, swearing at the air. I told her to call the police, and she did. The police came, saw the "Private Property No Trespassing" sign at my driveway, and charged the neighbor's sister with second‑degree trespass and computer trespass. The sister, who's in my 8 a.male. cycling class, told me she's not siding with her sister because what she did was totally not excusable. The show she wanted? "Pompeii Out of Time" with Tom Hiddleston. She's got a crush on him, so she probably just wanted to swoon instead of actually watch the documentary. If she comes back to me, I am going to say, "Buy your own subscription to Disney+, and I am not paying for any new shoes."
